subject: Interim: Cygnus-9b elevated 5xx/timeouts — stability update & next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@acmeapp.com>
Cc: support@acmeapp.com
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Cygnus-9b elevated 5xx/timeouts — initial notification

Hi Elena / Acme support team,

We observed an increase in 5xx responses and request timeouts for your traffic routed to model Cygnus-9b starting ~08:50 EDT this morning. Impacted calls are primarily generation requests with >2048 tokens and high sampling rates. We’ve put temporary routing in place to reduce impact while we investigate.

What we’ve done immediately:
- Enabled automatic fallback to the cygnus9b-quant variant for requests >2s latency
- Applied short-term rate-limiting on heavy-batched endpoints for your account
- Captured sampled request IDs and KV cache traces for triage (attached: cygnus9b-5xx-log-sample.txt)

Request from you: if you can share any request IDs or traces you captured around 08:45–09:05 EDT, that will help correlate client-side retries.

Next steps from our side: ops is running a focused triage and I’ll share a recovery/status update within 2 hours. We’ll schedule a post-incident call if you’d like a walkthrough.

Apologies for the disruption — we’re prioritizing stabilization.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Park <elena@acmeapp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 10:06:14 -0400
Subject: Re: Cygnus-9b elevated 5xx/timeouts — initial notification

Thanks Karthik — we saw the same failures and started internal throttling to reduce downstream retries. Attaching a small sample of client requests (acme-sampled-requests.json).

A couple of IDs we flagged: req-1427, req-1431, req-1439 — all timed out at 08:52–08:53. We didn’t change client configs during that window.

Please confirm if the fallback to the quant variant is expected to change model outputs in a way we should be aware of (short-lived hallucination risk, tokenization diffs, etc.).

—Elena
Elena Park
Head of Platform Reliability, AcmeApp
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 13:45:27 -04:00
Subject: Re: Cygnus-9b elevated 5xx/timeouts — triage & containment

Folks — quick ops summary and next actions (internal):

Observation:
- Spike in 5xx and timeouts correlated with long-context generation workloads. Error signatures point to an intermittent KV-cache thrash on worker nodes using the aten-cuda kernel for the attention matmul path.

Containment applied (done 09:00–10:30):
- Route high-latency/long-context requests to cygnus9b-quant which uses an alternate kernel and lower memory footprint (expected minimal semantic drift; communicated to client).
- Temporarily pinned a subset of requests to smaller context window when safe (app-level tweak).
- Rebalanced load away from affected GPU pool and drained noisy workers.

Mitigation in progress:
- Ops patch to KV-cache eviction heuristics is running in canary; we expect rollout to complete in next 2–3 hours.
- Engineering is preparing a hotfix for the aten-cuda kernel selection logic (INF-4872).

Attachments: mitigation-summary.pdf (contains timeline and traffic graphs).

I’ll coordinate an internal postmortem draft after the full RCA. We should propose (a) a customer-facing timeline + credits, (b) long-term kernel fixes, and (c) alerting improvements for early detection.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@acmeapp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:20:00 -04:00
Subject: Cygnus-9b elevated 5xx/timeouts — stabilization update

Hi Elena — quick update now that we’ve stabilized traffic for AcmeApp.

Status:
- The canary patch for KV-cache eviction completed at 07:10 EDT and the error rate for your traffic is back to baseline (~0.2% 5xx).
- We’ve fully drained the affected worker pool and rebalanced your capacity.
- For safety we will keep the cygnus9b-quant fallback active for 24 hours and then gradually return traffic to the primary variant after additional verification.

Root-cause (preliminary):
- An interaction between a kernel selection edge case and long-context KV-cache behavior caused elevated memory churn on a subset of workers, resulting in transient out-of-memory and 5xx errors. Engineering has a formal RCA in progress.

Next steps / ask:
- We’ve created a shared Drive doc with timeline and ops notes: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1Cygnus9b-RCA
- Proposed postmortem call: Fri 12 Mar 2027 15:00 EDT — please confirm availability and we’ll send a calendar invite.
- We plan to share a customer-facing RCA and proposed credit calculation within 48 hours.

Appreciate your patience — we’ll walk through the technical details on the call if helpful.

Best,
—Karthik
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@acmeapp.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 16:40:00 -04:00
Subject: Cygnus-9b post-incident summary (draft)

Elena, Karthik — following our call and the initial RCA draft, here’s the customer-facing summary we propose (short form). Feedback welcome and we can finalize for distribution.

Summary (short):
- Incident window: 2027-03-11 08:50–2027-03-11 10:30 EDT
- Impact: elevated 5xx/timeouts for a subset of Cygnus-9b worker nodes; AcmeApp observed increased client-side timeouts and retry behavior.
- Immediate actions: fallback routing to cygnus9b-quant, rate-limiting applied, affected nodes drained.
- Root cause (preliminary): kernel selection + KV-cache eviction interaction caused memory churn and intermittent OOMs on certain GPU workers.
- Resolution: canary patch to KV-cache eviction rolled at 07:10 EDT 3/12; engineering hotfix scheduled (INF-4872).

Customer commitments we propose:
1) A formal RCA and timeline within 48 hours (we’ll include request-level correlation and mitigation steps).
2) One month of reduced unit rate for impacted tokens or a credit equivalent; final calculation after we quantify token-level impact.
3) A joint postmortem follow-up call with engineering for technical Q&A (scheduled per your availability).

Attachments: cygnus9b-rca-draft.md (internal draft).

If you’re good with the tone and the credits proposal, we’ll finalize and send the formal letter.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
